III. A SPECIFIC STATEMENT THAT THERE IS NO FEASIBLE AND PRUDENT AL-TERNATIVE
Lincoln Highway presently passes through a heavily urbanized area where residential and business property has been built-up close to the existing right-of-way limits. Moving the proposed improvement to the north of the present location of Lincoln Highway would require extensive land taking through the heart of a substantial residential area in the city of Chicago Heights at prohibitive cost. The northern location would have required a large land taking from the Cock County Forest Preserve at the eastern terminus of the improvement. It would have also required a complete relocation of the Illinois Central Railroad Commuter station in the village of Olympia Fields, and would have required land taking from the village parklands west of Olympian Way.
Moving the proposed improvement to the south of the present location of Lincoln Highway would pose much no same problem as moving it to the north. Extensive residential land takings would be required. Also, large portions of two city of Chicago Heights parks would be taken for highway purposes. In the village of Matteson two cemeteries would also be extensively damaged.
Existing right-of-way through the Forest Preserve located at the corner of Chicago Road and Lincoln Highway is sufficient to construct the proposed improvement providing that the same roadway section used in the recent improvement of Lincoln Highway adjacent to this project on the east is continued. This section provides a 14-foot median and four 11-foot traffic lanes. The proposed improvement utilizes this section from the eastern terminus at Aberdeen Street through the Thorn Creek bridge and then tapers to a 16-foot median and 12-foot traffic lanes at Edgewood Avenue. This design will require no additional permanent right-of-way taking from the Forest Preserve, however a small amount of land will be needed though as a temporary construction easement for the removal of bridge wing walls over Thorn Creek and to provide a safer grade for the entrance driveway into the Forest Preserve District site. The improvement will minimize damages to properties on the south side of Lincoln Highway between Thorn Creek and Aberdeen Street, and it will provide a smooth transition between the normal roadway section and the completed improvement on Lincoln Highway which terminates at Aberdeen Street.
Relocating the improvement either north or south of the present Lincoln Highway location would pose severe problems. Extensive right-of-way takings would be required. Furthermore, Lincoln Highway presently acts as a natural neighborhood and school attendance boundary and any major change in its location would be disruptive to established community life.
